explanations.answer: All the Jews in the kingdom

explanations.answer: They don't obey the king's laws
explanations.explanation: That's his claim. Haman says, "Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws." Notice it's what Haman says, and it's the reason he gives for why the king shouldn't tolerate them. He's making his pitch sound reasonable.

explanations.answer: They refuse to pay the king's taxes
explanations.explanation: Taxes never come up in Haman's pitch. What he says is, "Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws." That's the whole charge in this verse. I'd keep the story to what the text gives us.

explanations.answer: So they would be ready on that day
explanations.explanation: That's what the text says. A copy was published to all the people "so that they would be ready on that day." The edict wasn't kept quiet. It went out to everybody in every province so the day would not catch them by surprise.

explanations.answer: So the Jews could flee in time
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about fleeing. It says the copy was published "so that they would be ready on that day." That's the reason given in the verse. I'd stick with that one, friend.

explanations.answer: So the king could change his mind
explanations.explanation: No second thoughts in this verse. The text says the copy was published "so that they would be ready on that day." That points to the day itself, not to the king reconsidering. The edict goes out to every province.

explanations.explanation: Not those two. It's the couriers who head out to the provinces. The text says, "Then the king and Haman sat down to drink." They stay put while the letters travel.

explanations.answer: They go to see the queen
